moduleTitle: Integrating Tricentis Testim with Continuous Integration (CI) Tools
learningObjectives: Explain how the Testim CLI enables integration with virtually any CI tool.
Identify which major CI/VCS platforms Testim integrates with out of the box.

elements.term: The CLI as the integration point
elements.description: Tricentis built the Testim CLI, installable via npm, specifically so tests can be integrated with CI systems. Because it's a simple shell command, it can be invoked from all major CI tools that can run a shell command — the CLI is what makes the integration broadly tool-agnostic rather than requiring a bespoke plugin for every CI system.

Testim integrates with Jenkins and other third-party tools including GitHub, GitLab, and Azure DevOps — some with dedicated, deeper integrations (branch mirroring, pipeline triggers) beyond just 'the CLI can be called from anywhere'.

elements.title: Full list of named CI/VCS integrations (Tricentis docs)

bulletPoints: The Testim CLI is a simple shell command — that's what makes it integratable with virtually any CI tool.
Named integrations include Jenkins (standard + Docker), Azure Pipelines, Bamboo, CircleCI, Codeship, TeamCity, Visual Studio, and GitLab.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Setting up and monitoring a CI integration

elements.description: The setup path is Settings > CLI > CI — from there, select your CI platform from a dropdown menu and copy the generated, ready-to-use command for that platform.

Once integrated, you can monitor test execution across builds from Testim and open the relevant test result with one click to diagnose a failure, plus review historical pass/fail analytics filterable by time period.

bulletPoints: Setup path: Settings > CLI > CI → pick your CI platform → copy the generated command.
Monitoring: one click opens the relevant test result for a build; historical analytics are filterable by time period.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming CI integration requires a unique plugin per tool
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Believing each CI system needs its own bespoke Testim plugin before tests can be triggered from it.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Because the Testim CLI runs as a simple shell command, it can be invoked from any CI tool capable of running shell commands — no bespoke plugin is required for basic integration, though deeper named integrations (Jenkins, GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps) exist too.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What makes the Testim CLI integratable with essentially any CI tool?

options.text: It requires a unique, custom-built plugin for every CI platform.
It runs as a simple shell command, which any CI tool capable of running shell commands can invoke.
It only works with Jenkins.
CI integration is not supported by Testim.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about the lowest common denominator every CI tool supports.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Because the Testim CLI is a simple shell command, it can be integrated with all major CI tools capable of running one — no bespoke plugin required, and it isn't limited to Jenkins.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which of these is a named CI/VCS platform Testim integrates with?

options.text: Jenkins
Microsoft Paint
Adobe Photoshop
None — Testim has no CI integrations

practiceQuiz.rationale: Testim integrates with Jenkins and other third-party tools including GitHub, GitLab, and Azure DevOps.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which of the following is NOT one of Testim's named CI/VCS platform integrations, per the official documentation?

options.text: Bamboo
TeamCity
CircleCI
Basecamp

practiceQuiz.hint: One of these is a project-management tool, not a CI/VCS platform.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Testim's named integrations include Bamboo, TeamCity, CircleCI, Codeship, Jenkins, Azure Pipelines, Visual Studio, and GitLab — Basecamp is a project-management tool, not a CI/VCS platform Testim integrates with.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the correct settings path to generate a ready-to-use CI command for a specific CI platform in Testim?

options.text: Settings > CLI > CI, then select your CI platform from a dropdown and copy the generated command.
Integrations > Test Management > CI.
Reports > Export > CI Command.
There is no dedicated settings page — commands must be typed manually.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's the same CLI settings page covered elsewhere in this path.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Settings > CLI > CI is where you select your CI platform from a dropdown and copy the ready-to-use, pre-filled command for it — no manual typing or unrelated settings page is involved.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Once a CI integration is running, what can you do from Testim to diagnose a build failure?

options.text: Nothing — CI results aren't visible inside Testim at all.
Open the relevant test result with one click, and review historical pass/fail analytics filterable by time period.
Only see a raw pass/fail count with no drill-down.
Automatically fix the failing test without any review.

practiceQuiz.hint: There's a direct link from a build to its underlying test result.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Testim lets you open the relevant test result for a build with one click to diagnose why it failed, and provides historical analytics you can filter by time period — it doesn't auto-fix failures or hide results entirely.

quickRecap.value: A shell command any CI tool can call — no per-tool plugin required for basic integration.
Jenkins (+ Docker), Azure Pipelines, Bamboo, CircleCI, Codeship, TeamCity, Visual Studio, GitLab.
Settings > CLI > CI → pick platform → copy generated command.
One-click test result access per build; time-filterable historical analytics.
